name: Look360
author: look360

sections.description:
Know the market before your customers do. Look360 (look360.eu) is a price and market monitoring service for online stores: it tracks your prices against competitors around the clock, watches your own store’s health, and alerts you to the price and stock changes that matter.

This plugin connects your WooCommerce store to your Look360 account in one click:

  • One-click pairing. Paste a one-time pairing code from your Look360 account into WooCommerce > Look360 and click “Connect”. The plugin creates a read-only WooCommerce REST API key for you and hands it to Look360 – no manual copy/pasting of API keys.
  • Findings right on your Dashboard. A widget on your WordPress Dashboard shows your latest Look360 findings and your price position against the shops you monitor, with a link through to the full Look360 dashboard.
  • Clean disconnect. Disconnect at any time from WooCommerce > Look360. This removes the local connection and the API key the plugin created; your Look360 account itself is unaffected.

What Look360 monitors for you

  • Competitor web shops: prices and stock levels, checked daily.
  • Competitor Facebook pages: campaigns and offers.
  • Your own store: price anomalies and other health findings.
  • Price comparison: see per product whether you are the cheapest, mid-field or the most expensive.

A Look360 account is required to use this plugin’s connection feature. The plugin itself is free; Look360’s monitoring service has its own separate pricing (see look360.eu).

Permissions

The WooCommerce REST API key created by this plugin is read-only. Look360 cannot use it to change orders, products, prices, or any other store data.

External services

This plugin connects to the Look360 service, operated by Watchdog OÜ, at scan.look360.eu, in two situations only:

  1. When you click “Connect” on the WooCommerce > Look360 settings page: the plugin sends your pairing code, your site’s URL (home_url()), a newly created read-only WooCommerce REST API key/secret, and your WordPress/WooCommerce/plugin version numbers to https://scan.look360.eu/api/plugin/uhenda/, so that Look360 can pair your store with your Look360 account.
  2. After you are connected, when the WordPress Dashboard widget “Look360 monitoring” is displayed to a user with the manage_woocommerce capability: the plugin requests https://scan.look360.eu/api/v1/leiud/ and https://scan.look360.eu/api/v1/hinnavordlus/ (authenticated with your Look360 API key) to show a summary of findings and price position. Responses are cached locally for 15 minutes to reduce requests.

No data is sent automatically in the background, on a schedule, or before you click “Connect” the first time.

Look360’s terms of service: https://look360.eu/tingimused.html
Look360’s privacy policy: https://look360.eu/privaatsus.html
sections.installation:
1. Install and activate WooCommerce if it is not already active.
  2. Upload and activate the Look360 plugin.
  3. Log in to your Look360 account at https://scan.look360.eu/konto/, open “WooCommerce plugin” and click “Create pairing code” (don’t have an account yet? Create a free one at https://look360.eu).
  4. In your WordPress admin, go to WooCommerce > Look360, paste the pairing code, and click “Connect”.
  5. Your Look360 findings will now appear as a widget on your WordPress Dashboard.
sections.faq:
Is this plugin free?

Yes, the plugin itself is free. Look360’s monitoring service has its own separate pricing – see look360.eu for details. A Look360 account (free or paid) is required to actually connect and see data.

Does this plugin give Look360 write access to my store?

No. The WooCommerce REST API key the plugin creates has read-only permissions.

What happens if I disconnect?

The plugin deletes the local connection and the WooCommerce REST API key it created. Your Look360 account and any data already collected there are not affected and remain manageable at scan.look360.eu.

What happens if I uninstall the plugin?

The same cleanup as disconnecting happens automatically: the WooCommerce API key the plugin created is deleted, and all plugin settings are removed from your database.

Where is my pairing code?

Pairing codes are generated in your Look360 account (scan.look360.eu/konto/), not in WordPress. Each code is single-use and expires after 30 minutes.

Is Estonian translation included?

Source strings in the code are in English (standard WordPress.org convention) and an Estonian translation is provided as languages/look360-et.po. This version ships the .po source only; a compiled .mo file could not be generated in this environment (no msgfmt/gettext tooling available) and is intentionally not included as a fake/placeholder binary. Compile look360-et.po to look360-et.mo (e.g. with WP-CLI’s wp i18n make-mo or Poedit) and drop it into languages/ to enable the Estonian translation, or let WordPress.org’s translation platform handle this after the plugin is submitted there.
sections.changelog:
1.2.1

  • Removed redundant load_plugin_textdomain() call (translations are delivered by WordPress.org automatically).
  • Uninstall hardening: the WooCommerce API key cleanup now checks that the WooCommerce API keys table still exists, so uninstalling after WooCommerce has already been removed no longer causes a database error.
  • Dashboard widget: when the Look360 API is unreachable, the failed result is now cached for only 60 seconds (instead of 15 minutes), so the widget recovers faster after a brief outage.

1.2.0

  • Public release on the WordPress.org plugin directory. Plugin updates are now delivered through WordPress.org.

1.1.0

  • One-click updates, served from the Look360 server (Plugin Update Checker bundled).
  • Dashboard links now deep-link to the correct Look360 account.

1.0.1

  • Added a “Settings” link on the Plugins screen row (points to WooCommerce > Look360).
  • Declared compatibility with WooCommerce High-Performance Order Storage (HPOS).
  • Translations now load on the init hook (WordPress 6.7+ requirement).

1.0.0

  • Initial release: one-click pairing with Look360, and a WordPress Dashboard widget summarizing findings and price position.
